references.text: The Sea of Kinneret (Sea of Galilee) is mentioned as a boundary marker, corresponding to the description of the Jordan border in Deuteronomy 3:17.
Describes the Arabah valley from Kinneret to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea), with the slopes of Pisgah to the east, the same geographical area.
Mentions Beth-Haram and Beth-Nimra in the Jordan Valley, with the Jordan as the border extending to the end of the Sea of Kinneret.
The Salt Sea (Dead Sea) is mentioned as a boundary marker for Israel's territory.
Describes the Jordan River stopping at Adam, the city near Zarethan, while the water flowed down to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea).
Describes the entire Arabah valley east of the Jordan to the Sea of the Arabah under the slopes of Pisgah.
The Valley of Siddim is identified with the Salt Sea, the same sea mentioned in Deuteronomy 3:17.
